clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond and your father Russell in secondary school, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time you began secondary school in 1987, three shifts piled up: distance from Desmond alongside your warmth toward your father, and anxiety when you made the city chess squad. Your stepparents separated that year over starting a family, and the household was unsettled; no one else's shifts show in these months.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: From early 1989 when your grandfather returned to the family after years away, through 1994, shifts mounted across several years with little settling between them. Your father's father came back into contact; your mother moved to rebuild the family home; you began secondary school in a cramped household and withdrew from activities. Your grandfather died in June 1991 during your first term at conservatory, where you injured your wrist and lost your footing in music; anxiety and functioning fell while you turned to your friend Rafe. By spring 1992 you were lost and low, grieving and uncertain. The trouble eased when you found direction again through film and left for exchange study in Lisbon in early 1994. Your sister Tara was born in the middle of this, and your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma nearby in time.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: In 1998 you and Joelle became a couple; within a year insomnia began to interfere with your work as a performer, though you were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions. You separated in July 1999 and started with a therapist that August. Two shifts count toward this time: your insomnia rising and your separation.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's diagnosis with bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: From 2001 when you began losing steam for performing alongside your grandmother's cancer diagnosis, through the winter of 2003, shifts kept rising and falling without settling. You ran out of steam and anxiety climbed; you had a disastrous audition and withdrew from your parents and friends. You moved away from Thornbury and began a new relationship in early 2003, then separated and sank into deep depression by that winter. You relied on friends rather than family, though your father and your friend Corbin spoke and gradually drew you back. You returned to your therapist and began to recover in early 2004. Your grandmother died in February 2004 after spending her final months in your parents' home. The visit you paid her then was brief and uneasy, and you regret it.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and your move to nursing school, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother's death in January 2008, you stopped speaking to your mother for roughly a year. That summer you went to work at Alder Creek and could barely manage a phone call with her; she pressed to visit despite your resistance, you kept the door shut on her, and once you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in August you cut off contact entirely. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation around the same time. The silence between you and your mother held until you returned home.

clusters.name: Your partner Wren's family arrival and your marriage, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: From your marriage to Wren in March 2017 through October 2019, a slow climb built in your anxiety and your sleep trouble. In 2017 you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; your anxiety over driving projects forward was your normal state by late 2019, and you started a sleeping pill. In October 2019 Wren's mother retired and the family gathered at the lake house: Wren grew swamped with events and you tightened a plan to settle her, though you would like her to cope without you. That weekend you had no sleep from the small hours and felt you didn't belong; Wren was anxious afterward on the quiet drive home. Your sister Tara was expecting her first child, and your aunt Imogen's memory was slipping worse. Your cousin Bella had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis the year before. Each shift in these months sits alongside your struggle with sleep and belonging when gathered with Wren's close-knit family.
